copyright_risks.content: The TV plays a clip that looks unmistakably like a scene from Breaking Bad -- a man in a yellow hazmat suit cooking in an RV.
copyright_risks.description: Direct visual reference to a specific, iconic copyrighted television series, including character design and setting. This constitutes copyright infringement of the underlying work and potentially the master recording/broadcast if an actual clip is used.
copyright_risks.suggested_fix: License the clip from AMC/Sony Pictures Television, or change the description to a generic 'TV show' or a fictional show to avoid specific identification.
copyright_risks.clearance_action: Contact AMC/Sony Pictures Television for clip licensing, or script revision.

copyright_risks.content: Also -- the soundtrack list still has three unlicensed Beatles songs on it.
copyright_risks.description: Explicit statement of intent to use unlicensed copyrighted music. copyright_risks.suggested_fix: Obtain synchronization and master use licenses for each song, or replace with licensed or public domain music.
copyright_risks.estimated_cost: Very high, potentially hundreds of thousands to millions for multiple Beatles songs.
copyright_risks.clearance_action: Contact the music publishers (e.g., Sony Music Publishing, Universal Music Publishing Group) and master recording owners (e.g., Apple Corps Ltd./Universal Music Group) for licensing.

trademark_issues.content: A McLaren 720S sits parked visibly on the street below.
trademark_issues.description: Visual depiction of a specific, high-end branded product. While generally permissible if incidental, prominent display could imply endorsement or product placement, requiring a clearance or product placement agreement.
trademark_issues.suggested_fix: Obtain a product placement agreement with McLaren, or obscure the branding/model number, or change the car to a generic luxury sports car.
trademark_issues.clearance_action: Contact McLaren's legal/marketing department for permission or instruct production design to obscure/change.

trademark_issues.content: Tell Nike we want the deal by Friday. If they walk, Adidas is already circling.
trademark_issues.description: Use of specific brand names in dialogue, implying business dealings. While often permissible, if the context suggests false business relationships, negative portrayal, or endorsement, it could lead to trademark dilution or false light claims.
trademark_issues.suggested_fix: Change brand names to fictional ones (e.g., 'Apex Athletics,' 'Stride Sportswear').

trademark_issues.content: His assistant, DENISE (30s), enters holding a Starbucks cup with the logo clearly visible.
trademark_issues.description: Visual depiction of a specific branded product. Prominent display of a brand logo could imply endorsement or product placement, requiring a clearance or product placement agreement.
trademark_issues.suggested_fix: Obtain a product placement agreement with Starbucks, or obscure the logo, or use a generic coffee cup.
trademark_issues.clearance_action: Contact Starbucks legal/marketing department for permission or instruct production design to obscure/change.

privacy_concerns.content: On top: a photo of a man who looks exactly like Elon Musk, unlabeled, mid-speech.
privacy_concerns.description: Use of a real person's likeness without permission. This is a violation of the right of publicity, which protects individuals from unauthorized commercial use of their name, image, or likeness. Elon Musk is a highly recognizable public figure.
privacy_concerns.suggested_fix: Obtain a likeness release from Elon Musk, or replace the photo with a generic 'tech mogul' or a fictional character's image.
privacy_concerns.estimated_cost: Potentially very high (if permission is granted) or $0 (if replaced with generic photo)
privacy_concerns.clearance_action: Contact Elon Musk's representatives for a likeness release, or instruct production design to replace the photo.
